greeting: Good morning, Bay View, and welcome to the very first Bulletin. Today there's a last call for a free community meal that's been feeding neighbors since 1994, a Thursday night show at Cactus Club, and Milwaukee's newest Cy Young winner. Coffee's on.

lead_image.alt: The Milwaukee Pierhead Light and Milwaukee Bay on a winter day
lead_image.credit: Michael Barera / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

top.title: Bread and Jam's free community meal ends its current run with a Thanksgiving feast
top.body: Bay View United Methodist Church (2772 S. Kinnickinnic Ave.) will serve its last free community meal in its current form on Sunday, Nov. 29, from 2:30 to 3:30 p.m., with a traditional Thanksgiving feast. The church's Bread and Jam weekly meal has fed neighbors since 1994, with food from Feeding America and volunteer cooks and servers from across Bay View and the South Side. Questions go to Pastor Anna-Lisa Hunter at the church.

image.alt: Flyer for the free Thanksgiving feast at Bay View United Methodist Church
image.credit: Bay View United Methodist Church via Milwaukee NNS

top.dek: The church's weekly free meal, running since 1994, ends its current form with a Nov. 29 feast.

top.title: Mayor's deadline for budget vetoes is Tuesday, and Bay View's street-light fix is in the mix
top.body: The Common Council's amended 2027 budget is on Mayor Cavalier Johnson's desk. He has until close of business Tuesday, Nov. 17, to sign it or issue vetoes. It includes our alder Marina Dimitrijevic's amendment adding money for library hours and roads, restoring electrician jobs, and creating a hiring bonus aimed at faster street-light repairs. It also includes a $1.35 million study of a possible city takeover of We Energies.

image.credit: Michael Barera, CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

top.dek: Johnson has until Tuesday to sign or veto a budget with more street-light repair crews.

development.title: We Energies rate hike approved, but smaller than requested
development.body: State regulators approved a smaller two-year increase than the utility had sought, its sixth hike in six years. The Common Council then voted 15-0 to fund a study of a city takeover of the utility, which still needs the mayor's approval.

image.alt: A We Energies building in Milwaukee
image.credit: Jonathan Aguilar / Milwaukee NNS / CatchLight Local

development.dek: Bills will go up again, by less than the utility asked; the Common Council wants to study a city takeover.

streets.title: Leaf rake-out extended two weeks, to Nov. 29
streets.dek: Late-falling leaves bought everyone more time: rake or bag them through Sunday, Nov. 29.
streets.body: Milwaukee DPW pushed the leaf rake-out deadline from Nov. 15 to the end of Sunday, Nov. 29, because many trees are dropping late this year. Rake leaves loosely into the curb lane with a foot of space from the curb and away from storm drains, or use paper yard-waste bags. After Nov. 29 crews make one final pass across the city, which takes two to three weeks, and snow can slow it down. Brush pickup requests close Nov. 30.

streets.title: Winter parking rules start Dec. 1: check your block now
streets.body: From Dec. 1 to March 1, there's no overnight parking on through highways and bus routes, and that includes Kinnickinnic Avenue. During a declared snow emergency, alternate-side parking is required citywide from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Fines escalate from $50 to $100 to $150, and repeat offenders can be towed. Sign up for the city's winter parking text alerts before the first storm.

image.credit: Michael Barera, CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

streets.dek: No overnight parking on bus routes like KK from Dec. 1, and snow emergencies mean alternate sides.

schools.title: MPS Superintendent gives her State of Our Schools address today
schools.body: Superintendent Brenda Cassellius is speaking this morning at Discovery World about efforts to strengthen Milwaukee Public Schools, including Bay View High and our neighborhood elementary schools. We'll recap what she says tomorrow.

image.credit: Michael Barera, CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

schools.dek: Cassellius lays out district priorities this morning at Discovery World.

schools.title: Last community meeting before MPS drafts its school closures plan
schools.body: MPS has one more community meeting before it sends a school closures plan to the board: Monday, Nov. 16, at 6 p.m. at North Division High School (1011 W. Center St.). The superintendent says closure decisions should weigh enrollment, building age, deferred maintenance and accessibility.
schools.dek: Monday's 6 p.m. session at North Division is the last before a closures plan.

protests.title: Nothing scheduled in Bay View this week
protests.body: We haven't found any rallies, marches or vigils planned within the neighborhood. Organizing one, whatever your cause? Send it in through the tip form and we'll list it.

realestate.title: Bay View housing snapshot
realestate.body: Bay View's median listing price is about $350,000, and homes typically sit 50 days and draw two offers. 17 homes sold in the past month, and four new listings hit the market this week.

image.alt: The historic Beulah Brinton House in Bay View

realestate.dek: Median list price about $350,000; 17 homes sold in the past month.

help.title: Ways to help this month
help.body: Volunteer for the final Bread and Jam Thanksgiving feast (Nov. 29, Bay View United Methodist). Give blood at the Bay View Blood Drive (Thu., Dec. 3, 2 to 6:30 p.m., same church; appointments preferred, walk-ins welcome). Or catch Saturday's God's Outlaw show at Club Garibaldi, a benefit for the Wisconsin Homeless Veterans Initiative.

image.alt: South Shore Park in Bay View
image.credit: Akaila of the Willows, CC0 / Wikimedia Commons

help.dek: Serve at Bread and Jam's last feast, give blood Dec. 3, or catch a veterans benefit show.

sports.title: The Miz is the NL Cy Young winner, unanimously
sports.body: The Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski won the National League Cy Young Award Wednesday night in a unanimous vote, capping his first full season in the majors. That season ended with Milwaukee's first World Series title.
sports.dek: The Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski won the NL Cy Young in a unanimous vote.

spotlight.title: Spotlight: URSA
spotlight.dek: The plant-filled lifestyle shop across from the library has been a KK fixture since 2017.
spotlight.body: URSA opened in the summer of 2017 in the historic King Building at 2534 S. Kinnickinnic Ave., right across the street from the Bay View Library. Owner Emily Kopplin hand-picks what fills the airy, high-ceilinged storefront: jewelry, apothecary and self-care goods, home décor, candles, prints, clothing and plenty of potted house plants, with many pieces from local makers. This week the shop has been posting its holiday décor, a fresh batch of ornaments and a new tote bag illustrated by a local artist, plus a closet sale of the staff's own clothes. URSA is open Monday to Friday 10 to 7, Saturday 10 to 6 and Sunday 10 to 5, and it also runs a short-stay rental, URSA Lodge.

image.alt: Inside URSA: shelves of home goods, pillows, bags and plants in a sunny storefront
